summary:
For some people, kindness does not feel comforting. A compliment gets brushed off, care from others feels uncomfortable, and self-compassion exercises feel fake. Psychologists call this fear of compassion, and it shows up particularly in people who are hard on themselves.

Our new blog by psychologist Natalia Cajide explains why kindness can feel threatening, and what a gentler first step can look like.

Equal Psychology offers psychology for adults and older adults in Kew, Croydon, and online across Melbourne.

Medicare rebates available with a GP referral.

Read the blog: https://www.equalpsychology.com.au/post/why-kindness-can-feel-threatening
